newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-German shares buck trend after forecast.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German shares buck trend after forecast.

text.p: German shares bucked the European trend and rose on Thursday after an economic institute reported business confidence slightly higher than expected and said it believed Europe's powerhouse economy could still qualify for monetary union.

The 30-share DAX index ignored a 0.5 percent fall in the Dow Jones average overnight and rose around 0.5 percent in early bourse trade, although traders said the market was largely driven by technical factors.
Traders said sentiment was underpinned by the dollar trading above 1.73 marks, although the foreign exchange market remained preoccupied by U.S.-Japan trade relations.
Europe's other two major bourses in London and Paris both declined in early trade, weighed down by Wall Street and local factors.

Germany's Ifo research institute reported business confidence a little above market expectations and predicted Germany's 1997 budget deficit would exceed the Maastricht Treaty's ceiling of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product by coming in at about 3.2 percent.

Despite that, Ifo President Karl-Heinrich Oppenlaender said in a speech prepared for the institute's annual meeting: "I nevertheless believe that with such a deficit, Germany will not be denied entry to European monetary union since the Maastricht Treaty allows certain divergence from the reference target."
Ifo said it expected German gross domestic product to grow by between 2.0 and 2.5 percent in 1997 but the average number of unemployed would rise by more than 300,000 to 4.3 million.
"The numbers support the view that the economic recovery is on track and that the economy is poised for expansion," said Armin Kayser, economist at Swiss Bank Corp in Frankfurt.

"I do not think there is much danger for inflation. The current recovery is unique in that we have the cost side, or wages, fixed for two years while the economy recovers. This is a favourable backdrop."
U.S.-Japan remained the main focus of the foreign exchange market ahead of a U.S. trade report due out at 1230 GMT and the start of the annual Group of Seven (G7) summit in Denver on Friday.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said overnight that leaders from the G7 leading industrial nations would discuss the risk that further significant increases in Japan's trade surpluses could undermine growth in other countries and trigger a backlash against trade liberalisation.
His comments followed a Japanese report on Wednesday that showed Japan's trade surplus with the United States and other countries surged in May.

"No one wants to go short ahead of the G7 but given that Japan's trade surpluses will continue to rise in the next quarter or two, there will be downward pressure on dollar/yen," said Paul Megyessi, strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
By 0945 GMT the dollar was quoted at 1.7304 marks and 113.16 yen, compared with 1.7289 and 113.32 in late European trade on Wednesday.
London's blue chip FTSE 100 index drifted lower as the market continued to fret over the new Labour government's July 2 budget and interest rates.
News of an 11.1 percent year-on-year rise in M4 money supply in May reinforced worries of ano in interest rates following Wednesday's strong retail sales figures.

"It's the monetary side of a very strong economy and maybe one on the verge now of overheating that needs controlling action to be taken. I think we should see a half-point increase in base rates at the next (monetary) meeting and I don't think that can be the end of the tightening in monetary policy this year," said Richard Jeffrey of Charterhouse.
With futures and options contracts due to expire on Friday as well, one equity trader predicted a weird and difficult 24 hours of trading.
"The market's going to move fast with a lot of trade in the derivatives," he said.
By 0945 GMT the FTSE was down 20.8 points, or 0.45 percent, at 4,636.2.
In Paris, French stocks were lower in early trade ahead of new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's keynote policy speech to parliament in the afternoon.
"The market's waiting for Jospin but also watching to see how Wall Street performs. The market's short on ideas for the moment," a trader said.
The CAC-40 index was off its lows but down 6.871 points, or 0.25 percent, at 2,744.87.
CURRENCIES AT 0945 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7304 marks and 113.16 yen, compared with 1.7289 and 113.32 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0945 GMN - The FTSE-100 index was down 20.8 points, or 0.45 percent, at 4,636.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 6.871 points, or 0.25 percent, at 2,744.87.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 19.78 points, or 0.53 percent, at 3,750.05.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $340.15 against $341.60 on Wednesday. Silver was unchanged at $4.73. Platinum was up $10.50 at $420.00, palladium rose $15.00 to $206.50.
